t: Section 602(a)(2) of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1995 (50 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2)) is amended by striking “improvement project to” and inserting “project for the improvement, repair, or modification of”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that changes wording in an existing intelligence authorization provision about construction or improvement projects. The tempting reading is that the underlying provision involves notification procedures, but any such notification runs to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The amendment itself creates no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: is amended by striking “improvement project to” and inserting “project for the improvement, repair, or modification of”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to statutory text, changing the definition or scope of a project type. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely legislative drafting.
qwen_block.s: Section 602(a)(2) of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1995 (50 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2)) is amended by striking “improvement project to” and inserting “project for the improvement, repair, or modification of”.

opus.w: This section only changes the wording that defines which construction projects the amended provision covers. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue. The provision it amends deals at most with notifying congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government, so even that would not count as participation.
opus.s: is amended by striking “improvement project to” and inserting “project for the improvement, repair, or modification of”
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** The tempting reading is to look at the provision being amended. 50 U.S.C. 3304 deals with notifying the congressional intelligence committees about intelligence community construction projects, which sounds procedural. But that notice goes to Congress, which is inside the federal government. And this section only changes the wording of what counts as a project. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part in any federal decision.
